trap-superlative.evidence: 'The unimodularity det T = -1 is a THEOREM ... not an assumption' — and it is false on one of the block's own three rows. Also 'All evaluated in milliseconds', an unprovenanced performance claim.
trap-superlative.notes: COMPUTED det for all three rows from the block's own T_j = [[c_j(q - q^{-1}) + d_j, c_j], [c_j, d_j]], with u = q - q^{-1}: pp (1, 0) gives -1 OK; nn (1, -u) gives -u^2 + u^2 - 1 = -1 OK; MIXED (1, -u/2) gives -u^2/4 - 1, which at proton q_0 is -1.010926552133130, off by 1.09%. Closed form -(q + q^{-1})^2/4, confirmed independently from the eigenvalues: sigma has eigenvalues q and -q^{-1}, so (1/2)(sigma + sigma^{-1}) has eigenvalues +-(1/2)(q + q^{-1}) and determinant -(q+q^{-1})^2/4; the two routes agree to 25 digits. The stated reason cannot work — det is multiplicative, so det(sigma) = det(sigma^{-1}) = -1 says nothing about the determinant of the AVERAGE (1/2)(sigma + sigma^{-1}) — and the failing row is the p-n pair, the one that matters most for nuclei. PROPOSED: restrict unimodularity to the pp and nn rows and record the mixed determinant as -(q + q^{-1})^2/4. On the timing claim: the .ts carries NO computation field at all, so there is no script and no witness behind 'milliseconds'. EVERYTHING ELSE VERIFIES: sigma^{-1} = sigma - (q - q^{-1}) follows from the Hecke relation; (1/2)(sigma + sigma^{-1}) = sigma - u/2, so all three (c_j, d_j) pairs are right; q and -q^{-1} both satisfy lambda^2 - (q - q^{-1})lambda - 1 = 0 with product -1; the degree bound sum (2 k_i + 1) = A(A-1) + (A-1) = A^2 - 1 and sum k_i = C(A,2); and THE DEGREE TABLE IS CORRECT IN ALL SIX ROWS, (A, C(A,2), A^2-1) = (2,1,3), (3,3,8), (4,6,15), (14,91,195), (56,1540,3135), (210,21945,44099), with every nucleon number matching its nuclide label.
